body.estimand_functional: \(\widehat\tau_k=\sum_{g\in E_k}N_k^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_g}(Y_{i,g+k}-\widehat m^0_{i,g+k}),\quad \mathcal C_{n,k}=[\widehat\tau_k\pm c_{1-\alpha,n}\widehat s_k]\)

sampling_model.design: Deterministic absorbing staggered adoption with the untreated cells missing by a nested staircase after each unit's adoption date.
sampling_model.units: A complete triangular array of deterministic low-rank mean panels with common regularity constants, fixed vanishing finite-slice rate envelopes, and jointly independent centered sub-Gaussian errors on \(\mathcal Q_n^+=\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}\cup\mathcal V_n\). Variances are time-invariant within units but may differ across units, and both \(N_n\) and \(T_n\) may grow.
sampling_model.treatment: The causal effect is added after \(G_i\); the target averages eligible treated units with unit-share rather than equal-cohort weights.
sampling_model.overlap: Every eligible cohort-horizon block has donor-row and pre-period Gram eigenvalues bounded uniformly away from zero after size normalization.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Exact Choi--Yuan blockwise nuclear-norm estimation and debiasing, leave-one-cell-out untreated residuals on \(\mathcal V_n\), unit-level residual variance estimates, plug-in influence coefficients, and a Gaussian multiplier summed only over \(\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: With appropriate debiasing, the proposed estimate is asymptotically normal even with fairly weak signals.
Event-time aggregation crosses calendar times and right factors, so its normal approximation and variance may differ from calendar-time inference.
The multiplier bootstrap yields asymptotically valid simultaneous inference for staggered group-time treatment effects under conditional parallel trends.
The data-driven intervals estimate each missing panel entry and match an instance-wise Bayesian Cramer--Rao lower bound.
The preprint gives heteroskedastic pointwise and nonasymptotic confidence intervals for individual effects and general scalar weighted bilinear treatment-effect functionals under staggered adoption.
The Gaussian and bootstrap approximation bounds are sharp in dimension and envelope for generic bounded high-dimensional vector sums.
Gaussian anti-concentration permits honest multiplier confidence bands without requiring a fixed extreme-value limit.

body.tldr: Choi--Yuan make weak-signal inference possible for structured MNAR blocks, but adoption-aligned event-time aggregation reuses donor and pre-treatment cells across calendar columns, so scalar variances do not determine a whole-path band. The project fixes the eligible-cohort unit-share event estimand, aggregates the exact Proposition A.4 coefficients into a growing-dimensional influence representation, records the resulting staircase covariance as supporting algebra, proves a feasible leave-one-cell-out covariance-rate theorem, and obtains an honest studentized Gaussian-multiplier band. Noise conditions cover the joint domain of influence and variance-training cells, while covariance and multiplier sums remain restricted to influence cells. An explicit finite rank-one two-horizon witness verifies normalization and produces correlation \(1/3\) from four shared cells. The exact attainable nonlinear-remainder frontier remains the first-class open question because the balanced strong-factor kill test indicates that the published norm envelope may be logarithmically loose.

project_justification.gap: Published low-rank MNAR results provide entrywise, scalar, or fixed block inference. Published staggered DiD results provide simultaneous event paths under parallel trends. Neither literature derives a growing adoption-aligned Choi--Yuan influence array, its shared-cell covariance, and a primitive feasible unit-heteroskedastic multiplier law.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a studentized event-curve theorem whose summands are primitive panel cells rather than cohorts, because one cell can enter several Choi--Yuan blocks and create persistent off-diagonal covariance.
project_justification.fill: The exact block coefficients are aggregated into one event-by-cell map, the Choi--Yuan perturbation ratios are bounded at each finite \(n\) by fixed vanishing envelopes over a complete-array class, and each finite optimization uses an explicitly induced slice. Residual-square training is confined to \(\mathcal V_n\), all noise conditions hold on \(\mathcal Q_n^+=\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}\cup\mathcal V_n\), and the feasible covariance and multiplier sums remain on \(\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}\). Gaussian approximation plus anti-concentration then yields honest whole-curve coverage. The open necessity node asks for the smaller attained remainder scale rather than declaring the coarse sufficient envelope sharp.

body.related_work: Choi and Yuan, \cite{ChoiYuan2024MNAR}, the main-text Noise Assumption, Proposition A.4, the staggered-adoption theorem, variance-estimation corollary, and Supplement G.2, supply the exact donor-row and treated-preperiod linear terms and primitive perturbation ratios. Their main-text residual variance is pooled, and the stated heteroskedastic extension remains scalar or blockwise; no cited result supplies a horizon-uniform unitwise variance-replication rate, so that rate is imposed here as a novel complete-array condition. Ben-Michael and Feller, \cite{BenMichaelFeller2026Discussion}, Sections 2--4, articulate the calendar-time versus event-time boundary, request staggered heteroskedastic inference, and document the 44-state right-to-carry application. Callaway and Sant'Anna, \cite{CallawaySantAnna2021DID}, Theorem 3, Corollary 3, and Algorithm 1, provide the closest cohort-time aggregation and simultaneous multiplier-band writing template, but their score arises from conditional parallel trends rather than low-rank MNAR completion. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato, \cite{ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2013Maxima}, Main Results 1--2, provide Gaussian and multiplier approximation for correlated coordinate maxima, and their confidence-band paper, \cite{ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2014Bands}, Theorems 2.1 and 3.1, identifies the anti-concentration scale at which a uniform nonlinear remainder affects coverage. Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Koike, \cite{ChernozhukovChetverikovKoike2023NearlyOptimal}, Theorem 2.1 and Proposition 2.1, sharpen generic approximation bounds and lower arrays, but their arrays are not constrained by one low-rank factorization and a nested adoption staircase. Yan and Wainwright, \cite{YanWainwright2024Entrywise}, Theorems 1--2 and Discussion, deliver instance-optimal entrywise intervals under staggered missingness, not an eligible unit-share event curve or its simultaneous law. Xia, Yan, and Wainwright, \cite{XiaYanWainwright2024ACA}, the abstract and introduction, pages 5--6, equations (2)--(4), Sections 3.1--3.3, and page 20, give heteroskedastic pointwise and nonasymptotic confidence intervals for individual effects and general scalar weighted bilinear treatment-effect functionals under a low-rank staggered staircase. Their result informs the scalar low-rank comparison; the missing object here is the joint growing-\(K_n\) law, estimation of covariance created by reused influence cells, and one simultaneous multiplier band for the Choi--Yuan eligible event curve. Xia and Yuan, \cite{XiaYuan2021LinearForms}, Theorem 1 and its alignment examples, show that low-rank linear-form variance depends on singular-space alignment, which explains why event-time aggregation cannot discard calendar-factor geometry. Choi, Kwon, and Liao, \cite{ChoiKwonLiao2024Completion}, the Feasible CLT and its displayed \(\widehat\sigma_i^2\) residual estimator, substantiate unit-specific heteroskedasticity for a fixed group-average functional; they do not supply the novel \(K_n\)-uniform replication envelope or a growing event path. Their rank-robust sequel, \cite{ChoiKwonLiao2026Rank}, Introduction and feasible block-average theorem, identifies a Tikhonov-type bias from rank over-specification, motivating the approximate-rank sensitivity seed without subsuming the exact-rank band kernel. Athey et al., \cite{AtheyEtAl2021MatrixCompletion}, cross-validation paragraph and Conclusions, establish the causal-panel nuclear-norm and random-cell validation baseline but not debiased simultaneous inference. Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein, \cite{BenMichaelFellerRothstein2022StaggeredSC}, linear-factor error theorem and Discussion, separate individual and pooled imbalance for staggered synthetic controls, informing the alternative combine-before-apply seed. Chernozhukov, Wuthrich, and Zhu, \cite{ChernozhukovWuthrichZhu2021Conformal}, exact-validity theorem and weak-dependence theory, give symmetry-based counterfactual inference; their route requires exchangeability or stationarity not supplied by the Choi--Yuan class.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The nominal Choi--Yuan envelope is obtained after several operator- and maximum-norm inequalities. In the balanced strong-factor rank-one calculation, the exact second-order terms are smaller by at least a logarithmic factor than this envelope under every symmetric split checked. This diagnostic prevents presenting \(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\sqrt{\log K}\to0\) as necessary. It does not affect its role as a sufficient primitive condition for the band theorem.
body.honest_scope: The settled target is conditional-mean event-time inference under exact low rank and independent unit-heteroskedastic cell noise on the full analysis domain \(\mathcal Q_n^+\). Serially dependent errors, approximate low rank, data-selected rank and penalties, and combine-before-apply efficiency are separate kernels. The staircase covariance formula is a supporting identity, while the substantive results are the uniform influence representation, feasible growing covariance rate, and joint multiplier approximation. The fixed-horizon reduction recovers the Choi--Yuan scalar result. The finite \(1/3\)-correlation witness is an algebraic sanity reduction, not an attribution of block independence to any published estimator. The model is a class of complete triangular arrays with common constants and fixed vanishing rate envelopes; every finite optimization uses its explicitly induced \(n\)-th slice. The exact attainable remainder modulus and the ordered under-envelope counterarray remain open in \(\mathrm{oeq:attainable-remainder-frontier}\); no sharpness claim is made for the coarse published envelope.
